speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry has plans to review polytechnic semester breaks so that they are aligned with the primary and secondary school holidays.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry has plans to align the semestral schedules of the Pre-Employment Training programme and Continuing Education and Training programme in the Institutes of Higher Learning.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This includes ensuring sufficient time for both curriculum coverage and student life during term time.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There are, however, overlaps between the term breaks of our schools and Polytechnics.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This better meets the needs of adult learners, who have to juggle both work and learning.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I would like the Minister for the reply.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Foremost, I would like to declare that I am an academic staff at Republic Polytechnic.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In December, for example, PET students undergo an exam period, that is, in December, they have the first two weeks of exams, followed by two weeks of supposed break.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: However, they are given graded assignments also, which means that throughout December, they are supposed to finish an assignment before they come back in January.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Which means, probably, that they will not spend their December holidays.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This means that they will spend less time with their family and catch-up with the younger siblings, if they have these.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: For CET students, the December period, especially for the part-time diplomas, that actually transcends throughout.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: For example, in December, their lessons are throughout December.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And this means that, for us to encourage them to do a part-time diploma and have a work-life balance, this means sacrificing their December holidays, and in the spirit of celebrating families, I think that this is something that we are missing.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The staff, they have to do the markings in December, which means they are usually affected.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I should perhaps lay down the following considerations on how we determine when we should go for breaks for different parts of our society.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because I do believe that different parts of our society do have different requirements and it is quite difficult for us to, therefore, have one model that fits everything.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I am quite sure that even if we do align it, there will be other challenges as well.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Second, I think we have to consider the different learning needs of different segments of our population.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, when we should have the term breaks for our IHLs is not just about what they learn in school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Companies would like to have interns according to their business needs, rather than just the academic calendars.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we need to take in to account all these differing needs.
